summary: This program builds a library of five Book objects, then walks through that list to collect each book's genre into a separate List<String> and prints the genres one per line.

lines.text: Two new books, Eragon and Fable, join the library, and both are Fantasy — that overlap is what makes the genre list interesting in a moment.
Creating a Book object and putting it in the list are two separate steps; a book only becomes part of the library once it is added to the collection.

The type inside the angle brackets is what a list holds, so this collection stores plain text genres while books holds whole Book objects. Two lists in the same program can hold entirely different types.
Each pass through the loop asks a book for its genre and appends that string to the new list, which is how one collection gets built from another.
The loop variable is declared as String here because that is what this list contains — using Book would not compile.
The \n escape prints a blank line before the heading, separating this section of output from whatever came before.
